description: Runs a run_trajectory request (without a readout) and compares one published quantity with the agent's measurements, each at a landed step. The answer is the error in numbers (rms, mean signed, greatest absolute, model minus measurement, each with its exact hex), the model value at every compared step in decimals (model_values) and exact (model_values_hex), and a hash of the measurements, under one seal. It sets no threshold: the numbers are the answer. The seal has no key, so it does not show who measured or who computed. commitment, optional, opens a salted SHA-256 the measurements were locked with before the comparison: data that are not the committed ones are refused before computing (CommitmentDoesNotMatch), and the seal covers it. genesis_seal verify-validation rebuilds the seal, the statistics and the commitment from the answer alone. In place of run, solves takes a plan of solves as run_dataset takes it (solver and plan, at most 64 solves), each measurement at a row of the plan: the solves are sealed under one dataset_seal, and the comparison by the same rules with the dataset_seal in the place of the run seal and the row in the place of the step; a measured row whose solve did not converge is counted in not_reached. The same request sent again gives the same seal. On this open connection a plan of solves holds the engine's own 64 and at most 15 s of them, or one, at each solver's measured time, which describe_solver states with the count (OPEN_PLAN_SECONDS). One address holds at most 1 physics permit at a time, and long work (a solve, a plan of runs or of solves, a run of more than 10000 steps, or a verification that computes one again) runs 1 at a time. A call that finds no permit or no place is answered "Too many concurrent physics tasks." and nothing waits: the same call sent later is answered once one is free. An answer is waited for 60 seconds, and long work is stopped there.

inputSchema.description: One run, or one plan of solves, and measurements of one quantity. The answer is the error in numbers, sealed with a hash of the measurements. It sets no threshold. A request holds run or solves, not both.

commitment.description: Optional: a commitment the measurements were locked with before this comparison, opened by this request. sha256 is the SHA-256 of these bytes: the line zero-trust-physics/measurement-commitment/v1 and a line break; the sealed form (the text a request's seal is taken over: keys sorted by their bytes, each number x and the 16 hex digits of its 64-bit float, no spaces) of {"component": <this request's component, or null>, "measurements": <this request's measurements>, "quantity": <this request's quantity>}; a line break; and the salt's bytes, its hex decoded. salt is 32 to 128 lowercase hex digits, 16 to 64 bytes, kept back until the comparison so that the data are not found from the sha256 by trying values. The engine makes the digest again from the request before computing: data that do not open it (a value, a step or a row changed, moved, added or dropped, another quantity or another salt) are refused as CommitmentDoesNotMatch, a salt shorter than 16 bytes as CommitmentSaltTooShort, a field of the wrong form as CommitmentMalformed, and sha256 or salt left out as InputMissing; nothing is computed and nothing is sealed. Opened, the comparison runs as it runs without one, validation_seal takes the commitment as a sixth part, and the answer says so in commitment_opened. A commitment shows that the data were not changed after it was made; when it was made is shown by where its sha256 was published before the comparison.

salt.description: The salt the sha256 was made with: 32 to 128 lowercase hex digits, 16 to 64 bytes.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 committed, 64 lowercase hex digits.

component.description: 0, 1 or 2: which of the three components of a 3-vector quantity is compared. Required when the quantity is a 3-vector, and refused when it is not. Any other value is refused.

measurements.description: At most 10000. A measurement is compared with the state after landed step k. There is no interpolation and no time matching: a measurement is placed by its step, its time since the start divided by dt_s.

row.description: With solves, in place of step: the row of the plan whose solve the value is compared with, numbered from 0. The rows rise strictly.

signed.description: An instrument's Ed25519 signature over this reading, by the rule run_trajectory's input schema gives at segments.

step.description: With run: the landed step the value is compared with. The steps rise strictly and none is past the run's total.

value.description: The measurement, in the unit of the quantity.

quantity.description: The name of one number the card publishes in its state, a plain name that has a '_hex' sibling in the state. A flag is refused.

run.description: One anchored run. Total steps must be <= 1000000. Recorded frames must be <= 10000. The shape of initial and of each segment's load depends on the pair: describe_card gives it.

card.description: The card of the pair, as list_cards names it.

domain.description: The domain of the pair, as list_cards names it.

dt_s.description: Step, in seconds. Held for the whole run.

initial.description: The phase fields of the card at the start of the run, each a number (a vector field is an array of three numbers), and no other key but signed: an instrument's signature over the rest of initial, under the key "initial", by the rule of a segment's signed. describe_card gives the fields, with each unit and bound.

load.description: The load fields of the card for this segment, and no other key. describe_card gives them, with each unit and bound.

signed.description: An instrument's Ed25519 signature over this reading, by the rule run_trajectory's input schema gives at segments.

solves.description: In place of run: a plan of solves as run_dataset takes it (solver and plan, a list or a grid, at most 64 solves). quantity is then one number the solver publishes in its result, and each measurement names a row of the plan, numbered from 0, in place of a step.
